title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, the Ministry of State Security, and the Ministry of Justice on Issuing the Provisions on Several Issues Concerning Strictly Excluding Illegal Evidence in Handling Criminal Cases
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate,
Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of State Security, Ministry of Justice
Issue the Notice on the "Provisions on Strictly Excluding Illegally Obtained Evidence in Criminal Cases"
Fa Fa [2017] No. 15

To the High People's Courts, People's Procuratorates, Public Security Departments (Bureaus), State Security Departments (Bureaus), and Justice Departments (Bureaus) of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court and Military Procuratorate of the People's Liberation Army; the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, the People's Procuratorate, Public Security Bureau, State Security Bureau, and Justice Bureau of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

On April 18, 2017, the 34th Meeting of the Central Leading Group for Comprehensively Deepening Reforms reviewed and approved the "Provisions on Strictly Excluding Illegally Obtained Evidence in Criminal Cases." These Provisions are hereby issued for your diligent implementation in light of actual circumstances. New situations, new problems, and new experiences and practices encountered during implementation shall be promptly reported to the relevant central authorities respectively.

June 20, 2017

Provisions on Strictly Excluding Illegally Obtained Evidence in Criminal Cases

For the purpose of accurately punishing crimes, effectively safeguarding human rights, regulating judicial conduct, and promoting judicial fairness, these Provisions are formulated in accordance with the Criminal Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China and relevant judicial interpretations, as well as judicial practice.

I. General Provisions

Article 1 Extortion of confession by torture, and the collection of evidence by threats, enticement, deception, or other illegal methods are strictly prohibited. No person shall be forced to prove their own guilt. In adjudicating any case, emphasis shall be placed on evidence, investigation, and research, and confessions shall not be readily trusted.

Article 2 Confessions obtained from a criminal suspect or defendant through the use of violent methods such as beating or unlawful use of restraints, or through the use of harsh measures amounting to disguised corporal punishment, causing the suspect or defendant to suffer unbearable pain and to make statements against their will, shall be excluded.

Article 3 Confessions obtained from a criminal suspect or defendant through the use of threats involving violence or serious infringement of the legitimate rights and interests of the person or their close relatives, causing the suspect or defendant to suffer unbearable pain and to make statements against their will, shall be excluded.

Article 4 Confessions of a criminal suspect or defendant obtained through the use of unlawful methods that restrict personal liberty, such as unlawful detention, shall be excluded.

Article 5 Where a criminal suspect or defendant makes a confession under the influence of torture used to extract a confession, subsequent repeated confessions made under the same influence of the torture shall also be excluded, except in the following circumstances:

(1) During the investigation period, where, upon complaints, reports, or discovery by the investigative agency itself, the investigative agency confirms or cannot rule out that evidence was collected by illegal methods and has replaced the investigators, and upon re-interrogation by other investigators, the investigator informs the criminal suspect of their litigation rights and the legal consequences of confession, and the criminal suspect voluntarily confesses;

(2) During the review of arrest, review of prosecution, and trial periods, where the prosecutor or judge, when interrogating, informs the criminal suspect or defendant of their litigation rights and the legal consequences of confession, and the criminal suspect or defendant voluntarily confesses.

Article 6 Witness testimony and victim statements obtained through illegal methods such as violence, threats, or unlawful restriction of personal liberty shall be excluded.

Article 7 Where the collection of physical evidence or documentary evidence does not comply with statutory procedures and may seriously affect judicial fairness, it shall be rectified or a reasonable explanation shall be provided; if it cannot be rectified or a reasonable explanation cannot be provided, the relevant evidence shall be excluded.

II. Investigation

Article 8 Investigative agencies shall carry out investigations in accordance with statutory procedures, and collect and obtain evidentiary materials that can prove the criminal suspect is guilty or innocent, or that the crime is minor or serious.

Article 9 After a criminal suspect is detained or arrested, they shall be sent to a detention center for custody in accordance with legal provisions. After the criminal suspect is delivered to the detention center for custody, interrogations shall be conducted in the interrogation rooms of the detention center. If, for objective reasons, an interrogation is conducted by the investigative agency outside the interrogation room of the detention center, a reasonable explanation shall be provided.

Article 10 When interrogating a criminal suspect, investigators may make an audio-visual recording of the interrogation process; for cases where the suspect may be sentenced to life imprisonment or death, or for other major criminal cases, an audio-visual recording of the interrogation process shall be made.

Investigators shall inform the criminal suspect that an audio-visual recording is being made of the interrogation, and this shall be noted in the interrogation record.

Article 11 The audio-visual recording of the interrogation process shall be made continuously, maintaining its integrity. It shall not be selectively recorded, edited, or altered.

Article 12 When investigators interrogate a criminal suspect, they shall make an interrogation record in accordance with the law. The interrogation record shall be checked by the criminal suspect; if the suspect is illiterate, it shall be read out to them. Where there are omissions or errors in the interrogation record, the criminal suspect may request supplements or corrections.

Article 13 The detention center shall register each summons for interrogation, recording the unit, personnel, reason, start and end times, and the name of the criminal suspect, among other details.

When the detention center accepts a criminal suspect, a physical examination shall be conducted. During the examination, procuratorial personnel stationed at the detention center may be present. If the examination reveals that the criminal suspect has injuries or abnormal physical conditions, the detention center shall take photographs or make video recordings, and the escorting personnel and the criminal suspect shall each explain the reasons. This shall be recorded in the medical examination record, which shall be signed and confirmed by the escorting personnel, the receiving personnel, and the criminal suspect.

Article 14 During the investigation period, the criminal suspect and their defense counsel may apply to the People's Procuratorate for the exclusion of illegally obtained evidence. Where the criminal suspect or their defense counsel provides relevant leads or materials, the People's Procuratorate shall investigate and verify. The conclusion of the investigation shall be notified in writing to the criminal suspect and their defense counsel. Where there is evidence that evidence was collected by illegal methods, the People's Procuratorate shall issue a corrective opinion to the investigative agency.

The investigative agency shall exclude illegally obtained evidence identified upon review, and shall not use it as a basis for requesting approval of arrest or for transferring the case for review and prosecution.

For major cases, procuratorial personnel stationed at the detention center shall question the criminal suspect before the conclusion of the investigation to verify whether there has been torture to extract confessions or illegal evidence collection, and shall make a simultaneous audio-visual recording. After verification, if there has been torture to extract confessions or illegal evidence collection, the investigative agency shall promptly exclude the illegally obtained evidence and shall not use it as a basis for requesting approval of arrest or for transferring the case for review and prosecution.

Article 15 For cases where the investigation is concluded, the investigative agency shall comprehensively review the evidentiary materials proving the legality of evidence collection, and exclude illegally obtained evidence according to law. If, after excluding illegally obtained evidence, the evidence is insufficient, the case shall not be transferred for review and prosecution.

If the investigative agency discovers that case-handling personnel have illegally obtained evidence, it shall handle the matter according to law, and may assign different investigators to conduct a new investigation and evidence collection.

III. Review of Arrest, Review of Prosecution

Article 16 When interrogating a criminal suspect during the review of arrest and review of prosecution, the suspect shall be informed of their right to apply for the exclusion of illegally obtained evidence, as well as their litigation rights and the legal consequences of confession.

Article 17 During the review of arrest and review of prosecution, if the criminal suspect or their defense counsel applies for the exclusion of illegally obtained evidence and provides relevant leads or materials, the People's Procuratorate shall investigate and verify. The conclusion of the investigation shall be notified in writing to the criminal suspect and their defense counsel.

If, during the review of prosecution, the People's Procuratorate discovers that investigators have collected evidence by illegal methods such as torture, it shall exclude the relevant evidence according to law and issue a corrective opinion; if necessary, the People's Procuratorate may conduct its own investigation and evidence collection.

The People's Procuratorate shall exclude illegally obtained evidence identified upon review, and shall not use it as a basis for approving or deciding on arrest, or for initiating public prosecution. Excluded illegally obtained evidence shall be transferred with the case file, with a notation that it is illegally obtained evidence excluded according to law.

Article 18 If, after the People's Procuratorate excludes illegally obtained evidence according to law, the evidence is insufficient and the conditions for arrest or prosecution are not met, it shall not approve or decide on arrest, or initiate public prosecution.

Where the People's Procuratorate's exclusion of relevant evidence results in a failure to find the alleged important criminal facts, leading to a decision not to approve arrest or not to initiate a prosecution, or a decision not to initiate a prosecution regarding part of the alleged important criminal facts, the public security agency or state security agency may request reconsideration or submit a petition for review.

IV. Defense

Article 19 Where a criminal suspect or defendant applies for legal aid, a lawyer shall be assigned from the legal aid system in accordance with relevant provisions.

Legal aid duty lawyers may provide legal assistance to criminal suspects or defendants, and may act on their behalf in complaints and appeals regarding torture to extract confessions or illegal evidence collection.

Article 20 When applying for the exclusion of illegally obtained evidence, the criminal suspect, defendant, or their defense counsel shall provide relevant leads or materials, such as the persons who allegedly engaged in illegal evidence collection, the time, place, method, and content.

Article 21 Defense lawyers, from the date the People's Procuratorate commences review of the case for prosecution, may review, excerpt, and copy evidentiary materials such as interrogation records, summons registration records, legal documents regarding compulsory measures or investigative measures. Other defense counsel, with the permission of the People's Court or People's Procuratorate, may also review, excerpt, and copy the above evidentiary materials.

Article 22 Where the criminal suspect, defendant, or their defense counsel applies to the People's Court or People's Procuratorate for the obtaining of evidentiary materials such as interrogation audio-visual recordings or medical examination records that were collected but not submitted by the public security agency, state security agency, or People's Procuratorate, if upon review the People's Court or People's Procuratorate determines that the evidentiary materials requested are related to proving the legality of evidence collection, it shall obtain them; if it determines that they are not related to proving the legality of evidence collection, it shall decide not to obtain them and shall explain the reasons to the criminal suspect, defendant, or their defense counsel.

V. Trial

Article 23 When the People's Court serves a copy of the indictment on the defendant and their defense counsel, it shall inform them of their right to apply for the exclusion of illegally obtained evidence.

The defendant and their defense counsel shall apply for the exclusion of illegally obtained evidence before the court session, except where relevant leads or materials are discovered during the trial. The People's Court shall, before the court session, send a copy of the application and the relevant leads or materials to the People's Procuratorate.

Article 24 If, before the court session, the defendant or their defense counsel applies for the exclusion of illegally obtained evidence but fails to provide relevant leads or materials and does not meet the statutory application conditions, the People's Court shall not accept the application.

Article 25 If, before the court session, the defendant or their defense counsel applies for the exclusion of illegally obtained evidence and provides relevant leads or materials in accordance with legal provisions, the People's Court shall convene a pre-trial conference. The People's Procuratorate shall, by presenting relevant evidentiary materials and other means, provide explanations regarding the legality of the evidence collection. The People's Court may verify the situation and hear opinions.

The People's Procuratorate may decide to withdraw relevant evidence. Evidence that has been withdrawn shall not be presented at trial without new reasons.

The defendant or their defense counsel may withdraw the application for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence. After withdrawal, without new leads or materials, no further application for exclusion of the relevant evidence may be made.

Article 26 If, at the pre-trial conference, the public prosecutor and the defendant or their defense counsel fail to reach agreement on whether the evidence was legally collected, and the People's Court has doubts about the legality of the evidence collection, the court shall investigate the matter during the trial. If the People's Court has no doubt about the legality of the evidence collection and there are no new leads or materials suggesting possible illegal evidence collection, it may decide not to conduct an investigation.

Article 27 Where the defendant or their defense counsel applies for the People's Court to notify investigators or other persons to appear in court, and the People's Court considers that the existing evidentiary materials cannot prove the legality of the evidence collection and that it is indeed necessary for the said persons to testify or explain the situation in court, it may notify them to appear in court.

Article 28 After the public prosecutor reads the indictment, the court shall announce the review and handling of the legality of evidence collection conducted before the court session.

Article 29 If the defendant or their defense counsel did not apply for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence before the court session but makes such an application during the trial, they shall explain the reasons.

In the circumstances described above, if, upon review, the court has doubts about the legality of the evidence collection, it shall conduct an investigation; if there is no doubt, it shall reject the application.

After the court rejects the application for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence, if the defendant or their defense counsel, without new leads or materials, makes another application on the same grounds, the court shall not conduct a further review.

Article 30 During the trial, if the court decides to investigate the legality of evidence collection, it shall first conduct an investigation during the court session. However, to prevent excessive delay of the trial, the investigation may also be conducted before the conclusion of the court investigation.

Article 31 To prove the legality of evidence collection, the public prosecutor may present evidentiary materials such as interrogation records, summons registration records, medical examination records, legal documents regarding compulsory measures or investigative measures, and verification materials on the legality of interrogation before the conclusion of the investigation, play relevant portions of the interrogation audio-visual recording, and request that the court notify investigators or other persons to appear in court to explain the situation.

The defendant or their defense counsel may present relevant leads or materials and apply for the court to play interrogation audio-visual recordings of specific periods.

When investigators or other persons appear in court, they shall explain the evidence collection process to the court and answer questions on relevant matters. The court shall stop questioning that is improper in manner or unrelated to the legality of evidence collection.

The public prosecutor, defendant, and their defense counsel may conduct cross-examination and debate on the legality of evidence collection.

Article 32 If the court has doubts about the evidence provided by the prosecution and defense, it may announce an adjournment to investigate and verify the evidence. When necessary, the public prosecutor and defense counsel may be notified to be present.

Article 33 After investigating the legality of evidence collection, the court shall decide during the court session whether to exclude the relevant evidence. When necessary, it may announce an adjournment for the collegiate panel to deliberate or to submit to the adjudicative committee for discussion, and announce the decision at the next court session.

Before the court makes a decision on whether to exclude the relevant evidence, the evidence shall not be read out or subject to cross-examination.

Article 34 Where, after trial, the court confirms the existence of circumstances of evidence collection by illegal methods as provided in these Provisions, the relevant evidence shall be excluded. If, based on relevant leads or materials, the court has doubts about the legality of the evidence collection, and the People's Procuratorate fails to provide evidence or the evidence provided cannot prove the legality of the evidence collection, and the possibility of evidence collection by illegal methods as provided in these Provisions cannot be ruled out, the relevant evidence shall be excluded.

Evidence that is excluded according to law shall not be read out or subject to cross-examination, and shall not be used as a basis for judgment.

Article 35 After the People's Court excludes illegally obtained evidence, if the case facts are clear, the evidence is reliable and sufficient, and the defendant is determined to be guilty according to law, a guilty verdict shall be entered; if the evidence is insufficient and the defendant cannot be found guilty, a verdict of not guilty due to insufficient evidence and failure to establish the charges shall be entered; if part of the case facts are clear and the evidence is reliable and sufficient, that part of the facts shall be determined according to law.

Article 36 The People's Court's conclusions on the review and investigation of the legality of evidence collection shall be stated in the judgment document, along with the reasons.

Article 37 The review and investigation by the People's Court of the legality of the collection of witness testimony, victim statements, and other evidence shall be conducted by reference to the above provisions.

Article 38 Where the People's Procuratorate or the defendant or their statutory representative files a protest or appeal, challenging the trial court's conclusions on the review and investigation of the legality of evidence collection, the second instance People's Court shall conduct a review.

If the defendant or their defense counsel did not apply for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence in the first instance but makes such an application in the second instance, they shall explain the reasons. The second instance People's Court shall conduct a review.

If the People's Procuratorate did not present evidence to prove the legality of evidence collection in the first instance, and the first instance People's Court excluded the relevant evidence according to law, the People's Procuratorate shall not present previously unpresented evidence in the second instance, except for evidence discovered after the first instance proceedings.

Article 39 The investigation by the second instance People's Court into the legality of evidence collection shall be conducted by reference to the above provisions on first instance proceedings.

Article 40 If the first instance People's Court fails to review the application of the defendant or their defense counsel for exclusion of illegally obtained evidence, and uses the relevant evidence as the basis for adjudicating the case, which may affect a fair trial, the second instance People's Court may rule to vacate the original judgment and remand the case for retrial to the original trial court.

If the first instance People's Court fails to exclude illegally obtained evidence that should have been excluded according to law, the second instance People's Court may exclude the illegally obtained evidence according to law. After excluding the illegally obtained evidence, if the original judgment's findings of fact and application of law are correct and the sentence is appropriate, the second instance People's Court shall rule to dismiss the appeal or protest and affirm the original judgment; if the original judgment's findings of fact are not erroneous but the application of law is erroneous or the sentence is improper, it shall enter a modified judgment; if the original judgment's findings of fact are unclear or the evidence is insufficient, it may rule to vacate the original judgment and remand the case for retrial to the original trial court.

Article 41 The review and investigation of the legality of evidence collection in the trial supervision procedure and the death penalty review procedure shall be conducted by reference to the above provisions.

Article 42 These Provisions shall come into force on June 27, 2017.
